thread:
Anita (Support): FYI escalated from CS — customer 'FinPay' reporting p99 API latency spikes since ~03:15 UTC for eu-west endpoints. they see large tails ~1.2s vs normal ~220ms. attached example request IDs and traces. can SRE triage?

Dave (SRE): Thanks. I see an alert for api.eu-west.p99 > 1s at 03:18. Correlating with TLS handshake time increase in our edge traces. Marking high priority. @Kevin can you grab tcpdumps / tracert from the affected edge pool?

Kevin (Oncall): On it. running quick curl to reproduce — hitting customer's org route:

```
curl -v -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" https://api.eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
```

Result (avg of 5): time_connect:0.12 time_appconnect:0.80 time_total:0.95 — handshake (time_appconnect) is indeed the bulk.

Rachel (NetEng): Noted. Could be cross-AZ or cross-region path causing extra RTTs during TLS handshake. If session resumption isn't being reused we pay full handshake cost. Any recent routing changes or DNS executor pushes?

Marc (Infra): No infra deploys in eu-west around that time. But cloud provider reports a partial route flapping incident impacting one of their POPs at 03:10 UTC. I opened ticket with them (INC-4892).

Anita (Support): Customer included traceroute from their side showing a detour through us-east before landing at eu-west edge. They said it started exactly at 03:12.

Dave (SRE): Can we get a traceroute from our edge to the customer IP and also from edge-to-edge?

Kevin (Oncall): Pasting traceroute from edge node eu-west-03 -> customer IP:

```
traceroute to 54.210.x.x (54.210.x.x), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  gw-1 (10.0.0.1)  0.2 ms  0.2 ms  0.1 ms
 2  infra-eu-a (52.1.x.x)  1.0 ms  1.2 ms  1.1 ms
 3  cloud-pop-eu (52.2.x.x)  6.5 ms  6.7 ms  6.4 ms
 4  core-isp (203.0.x.x)  42.0 ms  41.5 ms  42.3 ms
 5  us-east-gw (34.200.x.x)  120.8 ms  121.0 ms  120.7 ms  <-- unexpected hop to us-east
 6  customer-gw (54.210.x.x)  130.2 ms  130.0 ms  129.8 ms
```

Kevin (Oncall): That us-east hop explains extra RTT during handshake — adds ~120ms each way so ~240ms extra for first-time TLS. If multiple cross-hops or queueing, that can push p99 higher.

Rachel (NetEng): Two likely failure modes: (1) DNS resolution / EDNS returning non-ideal POP causing cross-region route, or (2) BGP path from our POP was temporarily prepended/announced that prefers transit via us-east. Marc, any BGP changes?

Marc (Infra): No config changes from our side. Cloud provider confirmed they had a partial POP outage and rehomed some prefixes causing traffic to hairpin through us-east. Their status page shows a short routing flap at 03:09-03:22. Ticket updated.

Anita (Support): Customer: they see it for both generate and embeddings endpoints, intermittently. They're asking for ETA and workaround.

Dave (SRE): Immediate mitigations we can try: 
- Force traffic for affected customer org to eu-west healthy pool (override routing weight)
- Enable aggressive TLS session resumption on edge (reduce full-handshake frequency)
- Increase keepalive and connection reuse headers for the SDK (we can ask customer to use keepalives)
- Fallback: route customer to dedicated eu region (if available)

Rachel (NetEng): I'll check if our edge supports session ticket reuse/OCSP stapling tweaks. We might flip edge TLS cache configuration. Quick check: edge config shows session_ticket: enabled, max_sessions: 0x400, but ticket-rotation was bumped earlier this month. Might need to increase cache size for eu-west pool.

Kevin (Oncall): While Rachel looks, I'll pin FinPay's org to eu-west pool explicitly to avoid the us-east detour. Doing a routing override now.

ops-bot: Route override applied: org=finpay id=org-9012 target_pool=eu-west-pool-1 by Kevin at 03:31 UTC

Dave (SRE): After override, let's re-run curl test from the customer's IP (via support's repro harness) and from our synthetic probe.

Anita (Support): Repro from customer's test client (post-override):
```
curl -v -w "time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}\n" https://api.eu-west.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Result: time_appconnect:0.28 time_total:0.42 — much better. Customer confirms faster responses for the last 10 mins.

Rachel (NetEng): Good. I'll still increase session-cache for eu-west edge to avoid handshake overhead for new connections: patching config now (will reload edge process carefully).

Marc (Infra): Confirmed cloud provider fixed BGP flap at 03:40 and route propagation normalised by 03:46. Their ticket notes 'transit path asymmetry' during the window. We'll keep the routing override off by default after stabilization.

Dave (SRE): Action items:
- KEVIN: keep override active for 30m, then monitor p99 for org. If stable, roll back (ticket INC-4892).
- RACHEL: increase session cache and add metrics to track appconnect breakdown (handshake vs data).
- MARC: follow up with cloud provider for root cause and ask for SLA credit if applicable.
- ANITA: keep customer updated and confirm they can move back to normal routing.

Kevin (Oncall): Will monitor. p99 for finpay went from 1.2s -> 410ms immediately after override. Setting a temporary synthetic check every 30s for that org.

Rachel (NetEng): Applied patch: increased session cache to 0x1000, session_timeout +10m, edge reload started 03:38 UTC. No errors in logs. Adding dashboards: tls_handshake_time and session_resumption_rate per pool.

Anita (Support): Customer replied: "Thanks, visible improvement. We'll keep an eye and report if we see any regressions." They asked for a short postmortem once root cause confirmed.

Dave (SRE): Postmortem notes (summary):
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 latency for certain customers hitting eu-west due to cloud provider POP route flap causing hairpin to us-east (03:09-03:46).
- Detection: SLO alert triggered at 03:18; support escalated at 03:20.
- Mitigations: routing override for org, increased edge session cache to reduce full TLS handshakes, provider incident follow-up.
- Long term: add automated detection for cross-region traceroute anomalies, automated per-org routing fallback if handshake component increases > 200ms, improve observability for handshake vs connection connect times.

Marc (Infra): Filing follow-up ticket with provider and ops finance for potential credit. assigning to cloud-networking team.

Kevin (Oncall): I'll remove override at ~04:05 if p99 remains < 500ms for 15m.

ops-bot: Route override removed: org=finpay by Kevin at 04:07 UTC

Dave (SRE): Post rollback check shows p99 during 04:10-04:25 ~ 320ms, handshake component ~0.18s. Looks stable.

Rachel (NetEng): Adding runbook step: when p99 spikes with time_appconnect dominant, run traceroute and check cloud provider status, then consider org-level pool pin before broader mitigations.

Anita (Support): Thanks team — I'll prepare customer-facing summary and let them know we'll share PM once provider responds. :thumbsup:

Kevin (Oncall): Closing thread once provider confirms. Good job on fast mitigation.

Dave (SRE): Agreed. Will add this to weekly incidents review.

(End of thread)
